title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data (United Kingdom General Data Protection Regulation) (Text with EEA relevance)
version_kind: point in time (dct:valid) of the version the site served as data.xml, saved by hand on 2026-11-26
converter: scratchpad script clml_dp.py, not deposited (tools are kept outside commons): the commons converter tools/fetch/fetch-source.py clml_text (last in commons at df75e54c2^) plus the additions of the Fraud Act 2006 deposit (key `converter` of subjects/uk/fraud-act-2006/registers/source-bundle/ukpga-2006-35.meta.json), whose code is carried over, plus the additions made for this deposit. Added: the Act's title, chapter number, long title and date of enactment as opening lines; the SCHEDULES divider and each Schedule's 'Reference' line; list enumerators ((a), (i), (1)); the number of a Schedule paragraph that has no heading and of every numbered paragraph after the first under one heading; the titles of sub-groups and tables; XHTML table rows, one per line with cells separated by ' | '; MathML formulas flattened to text; appended text joined to its line. Added for this deposit: (1) the structure of a retained EU instrument: the title lines (MultilineTitle), the recitals (each Division's number and text; recitals 19, 50, 71 and 143 carry their first paragraph in a Title element), the chapter and section headings (EUChapter, EUSection), the signature block and the annexes; (2) the 20 Official Journal footnotes: a marker [n] where each is referred to, and the notes themselves after the text under a 'Footnotes' line; (3) the in-force filter: an element whose RestrictEndDate precedes the dct:valid date, or whose RestrictStartDate follows it, is left out (0 in this file); (4) a trailing full stop in the number of a paragraph is dropped inside the brackets, so '1.' and '1A.' read (1) and (1A) (24 numbers). Dropped, as in the commons converter: editorial commentary (CommentaryRef, Commentaries), the contents list and the explanatory notes.
converter_checks: Controls: run on the Fraud Act 2006 XML saved 2026-10-21 (sha256 b3a267d809d0b3e1a6a872b29c4192bdd47515ca70d8335d3c46f6714a0c4107), this converter's output is byte-identical to the committed uk/fraud-act-2006 text (sha256 55201ca04f9d9a8dfad748c0f66e06ac4f39a873196bfafaea0db3a3e8e9557b). With the in-force filter switched off, its output on seven other Acts (Interpretation Act 1978, Companies Act 2006, Theft Act 1968, Criminal Damage Act 1971, Offences against the Person Act 1861, Value Added Tax Act 1994, Income Tax Act 2007) equals the 2026-10-21 converter's output byte for byte; with the filter on it differs on three of them (Companies Act 2006, Theft Act 1968, Value Added Tax Act 1994), where it leaves out 13, 12 and 6 end-dated elements. Completeness: every non-space character of the text under the EURetained element and of the Footnotes, outside the skipped editorial elements, appears in the output; 24 characters are missing, all of them the full stops dropped from paragraph numbers (see key `converter`). This checks that no text is lost, not its order. The same check first reported text missing: the first paragraphs of recitals 19, 50, 71 and 143, which sit in a Title element; the converter was corrected.
text_caveat: in-force text of the version valid 2026-09-30 only; no element is dated after that point and none was left out. Provisions omitted or repealed appear as the XML shows them, their number and heading followed by a line of dots (22 elements carry Status="Repealed", all checked to hold nothing but dots; 98 lines of the text are dots only); the former text is not in the XML. Amendment history is not in the text: the 477 Commentary notes of Type F (the notes that say which instrument amended or omitted a provision), 7 of Type C and 1 of Type X are dropped; the XML keeps them. No provision occurs in more than one version (no DocumentURI occurs twice) and all 129 elements that carry a RestrictExtent (the root among them) say E+W+S+N.I. Five effects that the XML records as unapplied (ukm:UnappliedEffect) are not in the text, and none was applied here. All five are word substitutions made by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provision) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/386), Sch. 3 para. 41 (commencement authority recorded as reg. 1(2)). Art. 57(3)(4): the file records the effect as wholly in force from 2026-09-30 and not applied, and gives no note on why; its only comment is an editor's instruction that two words ('Commissioner' and 'Commissioner's') are to be substituted where they appear. Art. 57(2), Art. 77 heading, Art. 77(1)(2) and Art. 80(2): the file marks each prospective, with the note that the amendment is not applied because s. 103 of 2025 c. 18 was fully in force before s. 119 (S.I. 2026/386 reg. 1(4)), and a comment that the amendment has no effect in that case.
